neighbours.label: the distinctive modifier of a technical term at the point where a passage names the concept it has just described (Haw[king] radiation, [flipped] classroom, [leakage] current)
fire: A black hole is not completely dark, because quantum effects make it emit a faint thermal glow. Physicists refer to this as Hawking radiation.
Pupils study the new material at home on video and spend the lesson practising with the teacher. This approach is called the flipped classroom.
Even a transistor that is turned off lets a trickle of charge through. This unwanted trickle is called leakage current.
The furnace burns coal in pure oxygen instead of air so the exhaust is nearly pure CO2. The method is known as oxyfuel combustion.
The drive stores data on flash chips and has no spinning platters. Such a device is called a solid state drive.
A liquid cooled below its freezing point without turning solid is in a fragile condition. Chemists call this a supercooled liquid.
Tiny particles suspended in water jiggle about at random as molecules strike them. This jiggling is known as Brownian motion.
Warm air trapped over a city by a lid of cooler air cannot rise. Meteorologists call this a temperature inversion.
quiet: A black hole is not completely dark, because quantum effects make it emit a faint thermal glow. Physicists were surprised by this result.
